html:
A Liberian social worker who led the Women of Liberia Mass Action for Peace, a movement of Christian and Muslim women that helped end the second civil war in 2003.

Dressed in white, thousands of women sat daily by the fish market in Monrovia, where Charles Taylor passed, to demand peace. When talks in Accra stalled, Gbowee and other women blocked the doors of the hall until the men reached a deal. The film Pray the Devil Back to Hell (2008) told their story. She shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 2011 with Ellen Johnson Sirleaf and Tawakkol Karman of Yemen.
sum: A Liberian social worker who led the Women of Liberia Mass Action for Peace, a movement of Christian and Muslim women that helped end the second civil war in 2003.
